source: RFC 0003 §4.4 F9, F10; RC1-50; review L1 of #1200; #1215; review L4 of #1231
statement: The periodic revalidation cannot be turned off or left unbounded: `cosec.authorization.snapshot.revalidate-interval` is at least 1 second, at most 5 minutes and, with fail-closed tenants, less than `fail-closed.max-lag`, or startup fails naming it (the lag thresholds are 6 and 30 intervals, `SNP-23`, so it is always below them). Installed documents are revalidated by periodic passes, each a conditional read of the store per document, never a local copy, and a reset of the change channel reloads them all. A pass starts every interval or, when the previous one is still in flight, as soon as it ends. A change written to the store before a pass starts, whose invalidation was lost or whose reload failed, is installed by the time that pass has finished with its document, whether or not a load of that document was in flight when the pass reached it: a pass never counts as its confirmation a store read that began before the pass did. It joins a load in flight only if that load started after the pass did; otherwise it waits for one more load after it, whose read is the pass's. A pass that has finished no document for `storeReadTimeout` and has no read in flight is abandoned at the next tick; a pass with a read in flight never is. A pass does not wait for a load of a document that has been in flight longer than `storeReadTimeout`; if that load started before the pass did, one more load still follows it, so the change is installed once that load's compilation ends, never only at a later pass.
guards: spring-boot:CoSecPipelineAutoConfigurationTest#a revalidate-interval that turns off or unbinds the periodic pass fails startup
